mainTopic: When a rumor (קלא) that a woman is betrothed is taken seriously or ignored: קטן cases, אמתלא, rumors after אירוסין, and a rumor followed by a second betrothal
overview: This amud keeps asking when a rumor (קלא) that a woman is betrothed can be ignored. רבא says a rumor about 'one of the sons of so-and-so' is set aside, because people will assume it was the betrothal of a קטן. A boy who only looks grown-up is still a קטן, so a rumor about him also means nothing. Next the גמרא explains the משנה's condition about an אמתלא, an innocent explanation. רב זביד says a reasonable explanation counts even if nobody said it. רב כהנא tries to support him from a משנה in יבמות, but the גמרא pushes that proof away. רב אשי then teaches that a rumor counts only if it was confirmed in בית דין, and the הלכה is that a rumor that comes up after אירוסין is ignored. Finally, שמואל rules on a rumor of a first betrothal followed by a definite second one, and the אמוראים debate which man must give a גט and which may marry her when the facts stay unclear.

steps.title: A rumor about 'one of the sons' is set aside
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that a rumor that a woman was betrothed to an unnamed son of a certain man is set aside, because people will assume it was a קטן's betrothal.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a rumor that a woman was betrothed to one of a certain man's sons. רבא said: even the opinion that we do not set aside a rumor agrees that here we do. People will say that the רבנן looked into the betrothal and found it was the betrothal of a קטן, which means nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a ruling about a rumor that a woman was betrothed to one of someone's sons, without saying which son.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually there is a debate about whether a rumor can be cancelled once it spreads. רבא says that here everyone agrees it can, because the rumor is vague and some of the sons may be young. When the rumor is set aside, people will not suspect wrongdoing. They will simply assume the betrothal belonged to a קטן and was never valid.

keyTerms.meaning: Betrothal by a minor boy, which has no legal force

phrases.english: to one of the sons of so-and-so,
Rava said: Even according to the one who says
we do not set aside a rumor,
in this case we set aside the rumor;

phrases.aramaic: מֵימָר אָמְרִי: עַיִּינוּ בְּהוּ רַבָּנַן בְּקִידּוּשֵׁי,
phrases.english: for people will say: the Rabbis looked into the betrothal,
and it was the betrothal of a minor.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: אֲפִילּוּ לְמַאן דְּאָמַר לָא מְבַטְּלִינַן קָלָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion of whether a rumor of betrothal can be set aside.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A rumor of betrothal to an unnamed son of so-and-so is set aside, even according to the view that rumors are normally not set aside.

steps.title: A minor who looks like an adult
steps.stepSummary: A rumor said a woman was betrothed to a קטן who looked grown-up. רב מרדכי cites a precedent: he has not yet reached adult understanding, so the betrothal is nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: A rumor spread that a woman was betrothed to a minor who looked like an adult. רב מרדכי told רב אשי that this had already happened, and the רבנן said: he has not yet reached 'the divisions of ראובן.' The פסוק says, 'Among the divisions of ראובן there were great resolves of heart,' which means real grown-up understanding.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new case: a rumor of betrothal to a boy who is a קטן but looks like an adult. רב מרדכי answers from an earlier real case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might think that because the boy looks grown-up, people will treat the betrothal as real. The precedent teaches that a grown-up body is not enough. Without adult understanding, which the פסוק calls 'resolves of heart,' his betrothal is not valid, so the rumor does not bind her.

keyTerms.meaning: A minor who looks like an adult
A real case that happened, a precedent
The divisions of ראובן; used here to mean adult understanding
Resolves or searchings of the heart, meaning mature thinking

steps.whatToRemember: Looking grown-up does not make a קטן an adult. He still lacks the mature mind needed for betrothal.

phrases.english: A certain woman about whom a rumor went out,
that she was betrothed to a minor who looked like an adult.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב מָרְדֳּכַי לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Mordekhai said to Rav Ashi:
There was such a case, and they said:
He has not yet reached 'the divisions of Reuben,'
as it is stated: 'Among the divisions of Reuben
there were great resolves of heart.'

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהִיא דִּנְפַק עֲלַהּ קָלָא, דְּאִיקַּדַּשָׁה לְקָטָן הַנִּרְאֶה כְּגָדוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another case of a rumor connected to a קטן, decided by a precedent.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A קטן who looks like an adult still lacks adult understanding, so a rumor that he betrothed a woman is disregarded.

steps.title: An explanation counts even ten days later
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's condition 'provided there is no אמתלא.' רבה בר רב הונא says an explanation counts even if it comes up within ten days.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said the rumor is taken seriously only if there is no אמתלא, an explanation that weakens it. רבה בר רב הונא said: the explanation the רבנן spoke about works even if it comes up any time from now until ten days later.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now goes back to a phrase in the משנה and begins explaining what kind of אמתלא cancels a rumor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אמתלא is a story that shows the rumor is not really a sign of a valid betrothal. רבה בר רב הונא teaches that the explanation does not have to show up together with the rumor. Even if it comes up as late as ten days afterward, it still cancels the rumor.

keyTerms.meaning: An explanation or excuse that weakens a rumor
From now until ten days later

phrases.english: 'Provided there is no explanation there':

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא: אֲמַתְלָא שֶׁאָמְרוּ,
phrases.english: Rabba bar Rav Huna said: The explanation that they spoke of
works even from now until ten days later.
phrases.notes: He means: even if the explanation comes up only within ten days after the rumor.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבִלְבַד שֶׁלֹּא תְּהֵא שָׁם אֲמַתְלָא: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the rumor cases to explaining the משנה's אמתלא condition.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An explanation that comes up within ten days of the rumor still cancels it.

steps.title: A reasonable explanation counts even if unsaid
steps.stepSummary: רב זביד says that wherever an explanation is reasonable, we take it into account even if no one actually said it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב זביד said: in a situation where an explanation is reasonable, we take that explanation into account.
steps.whatsHappening: רב זביד gives a second, broader view of how an אמתלא works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה בר רב הונא spoke about an explanation that someone actually gives, even if late. רב זביד goes further: if the situation makes an innocent explanation likely, we consider it even if nobody said it. So the rumor is set aside more easily.

keyTerms.meaning: In a situation where an explanation is possible
We take into account, we are concerned about

phrases.english: Rav Zevid says:
Where there is room for an explanation, we take the explanation into account.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב זְבִיד אָמַר: בִּמְקוֹם אֲמַתְלָא, חוֹשְׁשִׁין לַאֲמַתְלָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A different, broader approach to the same משנה phrase.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Where an explanation is reasonable, it is considered even if not stated, and the rumor is set aside.

steps.title: רב פפא challenges from the משנה's wording
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא challenges רב זביד: the משנה says 'provided there is no explanation there,' which sounds like the explanation must actually be present.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא raised an objection to רב זביד from the משנה: 'Provided there is no explanation there!'
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא attacks רב זביד's view using the exact words of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'there is no explanation there' sound like they describe an explanation that was actually said. If so, an unspoken explanation that is only possible should not count. That goes against רב זביד.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa raised an objection to Rav Zevid:
'Provided there is no explanation there!'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב זביד's statement.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב זביד's rule that a possible but unspoken explanation is taken into account
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's wording seems to require an explanation that is actually present, not one that is only possible.

steps.title: רב זביד: the משנה means a possible explanation
steps.stepSummary: רב זביד answers that the משנה is talking about a situation where an explanation is possible, which is his own view.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב זביד said to him: the משנה is speaking about a situation where an explanation is possible.
steps.whatsHappening: רב זביד answers the challenge by reading the משנה's words in line with his view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב זביד reads 'there is no explanation there' as 'there is no room for an explanation.' So the משנה only takes the rumor seriously when no innocent explanation is reasonable. The משנה's words fit his opinion after all.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רב זביד, a rumor is set aside whenever an innocent explanation is reasonable, even if no one actually said it.

phrases.english: He said to him: It is speaking of a situation where an explanation is possible.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב פפא's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה requires an explanation that was actually given.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה means a situation where an explanation is reasonable, even if it was not stated.

steps.title: רב כהנא brings a משנה that seems to support רב זביד
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא challenges רב פפא with a משנה: a woman who was betrothed to a second man, and then her first husband returned, may go back to him. That seems to be because we assume the second betrothal was conditional, even though nobody said so.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said to רב פפא: Don't you agree with רב זביד? We learned in a משנה that if a woman was betrothed to another man and then her missing husband came back, she may return to him. Isn't that because we say the second man betrothed her on a condition, even though no one actually said it?
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא pushes back on רב פפא and uses a משנה to back up רב זביד's idea that an unspoken but reasonable explanation counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, nobody said the second betrothal was conditional, yet the woman may go back to her husband. רב כהנא reads this as the משנה assuming a sensible condition on its own. That is just what רב זביד said: a reasonable explanation counts even if no one said it.

keyTerms.meaning: And you, don't you hold this?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב כָּהֲנָא לְרַב פָּפָּא:
phrases.english: Rav Kahana said to Rav Pappa:
And you, don't you hold this?!
phrases.notes: He means רב זביד's idea that a reasonable explanation counts even if nobody said it.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָתְנַן: נִתְקַדְּשָׁה, וְאַחַר כָּךְ בָּא בַּעְלָהּ –
phrases.english: But didn't we learn: if she was betrothed, and afterward her husband came back –
phrases.notes: This משנה is in יבמות. It is about a woman whose husband was thought to be dead.

phrases.english: she is permitted to return to him.

phrases.aramaic: לָאו מִשּׁוּם דְּאָמְרִינַן עַל תְּנַאי קַדֵּישׁ?
phrases.english: Isn't that because we say he betrothed her on a condition?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב כָּהֲנָא לְרַב פָּפָּא: וְאַתְּ לָא תִּסְבְּרַאּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the רב זביד and רב פפא debate. It brings outside proof for רב זביד against רב פפא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's position that only an explanation actually present counts
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה lets a woman return to her husband because we assume a condition nobody said. So unspoken but reasonable explanations do count.
steps.raayaObject: רב זביד's rule that a reasonable explanation counts even if not said
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in יבמות: נתקדשה ואחר כך בא בעלה מותרת לחזור

steps.title: That case is different because the husband protests
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes the proof away. In the משנה the husband himself shows up and protests, so it is clear the betrothal was a mistake. We do not need to assume any hidden condition.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there, because the husband comes and protests.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רב כהנא by showing that the משנה's case has a different reason behind it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the first husband comes back and objects, everyone sees he never divorced her. The second betrothal falls apart because of that clear fact, not because of an assumed explanation. So the משנה does not prove רב זביד's rule.

phrases.english: It is different there,
because the husband comes and protests.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 7 by limiting the משנה to a special case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה relies on an unspoken condition, which would support רב זביד.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה relies on the husband's open protest, so it proves nothing about unspoken explanations.

steps.title: Then she should be allowed back even after marrying
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if the husband's protest is enough, the same should be true if she fully married the second man. Yet the משנה forbids her to return in that case.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, she should also be allowed back if she married the second man!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the answer from step 8 by applying it to the case of a woman who fully married.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The husband protests just as much when she has married someone else. If his protest makes her permitted to return, it should work there too. But the משנה forbids her to return after marrying, so the answer seems too broad.

phrases.english: If so, if she married, also!
phrases.notes: He means she should be allowed to go back to her husband in that case too.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the husband's protest is the reason she may return
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The husband protests in the marriage case too, yet there she may not return. So his protest cannot be the full reason.

steps.title: A married woman was penalized; a betrothed one was not
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the difference. When she married, she lived with another man while still married, which is forbidden, so the רבנן penalized her. When she was only betrothed, she did nothing forbidden, so there was no penalty.
steps.simpleTranslation: When she married, she did a forbidden act, so the רבנן penalized her. When she was only betrothed, she did no forbidden act, so the רבנן did not penalize her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question of step 9 by giving a separate reason why the married woman may not return.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In both cases the husband's protest shows the second union was a mistake. The difference is a penalty (קנס). The married woman actually lived with another man, even if by accident, so the רבנן penalized her. The betrothed woman never did that, so she keeps her right to return.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה about a woman whose husband returned does not prove רב זביד. She may return after אירוסין because the husband protests, and she may not return after נישואין because of a rabbinic penalty.

phrases.english: If she married, since she did a forbidden act –
the רבנן penalized her;
if she was only betrothed, since she did not do a forbidden act –
the רבנן did not penalize her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different reason for each case (a rabbinic penalty)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The husband's protest should permit her to return in both cases.
steps.terutzMaskana: It does permit her in both, but after נישואין the רבנן added a penalty because she did a forbidden act.

steps.title: A rumor not confirmed in court is not a rumor
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי teaches that a rumor only matters if it was confirmed in בית דין. Without that, it is not counted as a rumor at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Any rumor that was not confirmed in בית דין is not a rumor.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic and gives רב אשי's rule about which rumors count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the topic was rumors that a woman was betrothed. רב אשי adds a limit: talk among people is not enough. Only a rumor that was confirmed in בית דין has any legal weight.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule makes it much harder for loose talk to change a woman's status.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל קָלָא דְּלָא אִיתַּחְזַק בְּבֵי דִינָא –
phrases.english: Any rumor that was not confirmed in court –
is not a rumor.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: כֹּל קָלָא דְּלָא אִיתַּחְזַק בְּבֵי דִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new set of rulings about rumors.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A rumor counts only if it was confirmed in בית דין.

steps.title: A rumor after marriage is ignored, but not one after betrothal
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי gives a second rule. If a rumor comes up after the woman is fully married, we ignore it. The גמרא then infers from his words that a rumor coming up after only אירוסין is taken seriously.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב אשי said: Any rumor that comes up after נישואין, we are not concerned about it. This implies that one that comes up after אירוסין, we are concerned about it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי teaches a second rule, and the גמרא draws an inference from it about rumors after אירוסין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once she is fully married, a late rumor does not make her leave her husband. The words 'after marriage' imply that the rule is different after אירוסין alone. In that case we do worry about the rumor, and she would need a גט from her betrothed.

keyTerms.meaning: Betrothal, the first stage of marriage
We are concerned, we take it into account

steps.confusionAlert: The words 'הא דבתר אירוסין חיישינן ליה' are not a separate statement by רב אשי. The גמרא is drawing them out of his words.

phrases.english: And Rav Ashi said:
Any rumor that comes after marriage –
we are not concerned about it;
this implies that one after betrothal –
we are concerned about it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: כֹּל קָלָא דְּבָתַר נִישּׂוּאִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second rule by the same speaker, רב אשי, on the same topic of rumors.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A rumor after נישואין is ignored. By implication, a rumor after אירוסין is taken into account.

steps.title: רב חביבא: even after betrothal we ignore the rumor
steps.stepSummary: רב חביבא disagrees with the inference from רב אשי. He says that even a rumor that comes up after only אירוסין is ignored.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חביבא said: Even a rumor after אירוסין, we are also not concerned about it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חביבא gives a different view from the one implied in רב אשי's words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי's words imply that a rumor after אירוסין matters. רב חביבא extends the leniency: once the woman is betrothed, a later rumor does not count, even before full marriage.

phrases.english: Rav Chaviva said:
Even one after betrothal, also,
we are not concerned about it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב חֲבִיבָא אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ דְּבָתַר אֵירוּסִין נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the inference drawn from רב אשי in step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A rumor that comes up after אירוסין is also ignored.

steps.title: The הלכה: we ignore the rumor
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא decides the הלכה like רב חביבא: we do not worry about a rumor that comes up after אירוסין.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is: we are not concerned about it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends the discussion by deciding the practical הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Of the two views about a rumor after אירוסין, the גמרא follows רב חביבא. A rumor that comes up after the woman is already betrothed is ignored, just like one after נישואין.
steps.whatToRemember: A rumor counts only if confirmed in בית דין. A rumor that comes up after the woman is already betrothed or married is ignored, following רב חביבא.

phrases.english: And the halakha is: we are not concerned about it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides between the inference from רב אשי (step 12) and רב חביבא (step 13).
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows רב חביבא: a rumor after אירוסין is not taken into account.

steps.title: The question sent to שמואל about a rumor followed by a real betrothal
steps.stepSummary: רב ירמיה בר אבא reports that רב's students asked שמואל what happens when a woman has a rumor of a first betrothal and then a second man betroths her properly.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ירמיה בר אבא said: The students of רב sent a question to שמואל: 'Teach us, our master. A rumor went around that a woman was betrothed to a first man. Then another man came and gave her a betrothal that is valid by Torah law. What is the law?'
steps.whatsHappening: A new case is brought. The students of רב ask שמואל what to do when a woman has a rumor of a first betrothal and then receives a definite second betrothal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first betrothal is only a קול, a rumor. The second betrothal is definite, with clear witnesses. The question is whether a weak rumor can outweigh a certain, Torah-valid קידושין.

keyTerms.meaning: The study hall of רב, meaning his students
'Let our master teach us', a polite way of opening a question
A betrothal that is fully valid by Torah law

phrases.english: Rav Yirmeya bar Abba said:
They sent from the house of Rav to Shmuel:
Let our master teach us:
A rumor went out about her that she was betrothed to a first man,
and another man came and betrothed her
with a Torah-valid betrothal. What is the law?
phrases.notes: 'Torah-valid' here means the second betrothal is definite, done with clear witnesses.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלַחוּ לֵיהּ מִבֵּי רַב לִשְׁמוּאֵל, יְלַמְּדֵנוּ רַבֵּינוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the rules about when a rumor counts to a new case: a rumor followed by a definite betrothal from a second man.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a rumor of a first betrothal affect a woman who later received a definite Torah betrothal from someone else?

steps.title: שמואל: she must leave, clarify the facts, and report back
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that she must leave the second man, and they should investigate the matter and tell him the result.
steps.simpleTranslation: He sent back to them: 'She must leave the second man. Clarify the matter fully, and let me know.'
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל answers. For now she must separate from the second man, and the facts must be checked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל takes the rumor seriously enough to separate her from the second man, even though his betrothal is definite. He does not give a final ruling yet. He wants the facts first.

keyTerms.meaning: He sent to them (a written answer)
She must leave (separate from the second man)

phrases.english: He sent to them: She must leave,
and clarify the matter thoroughly,
and let me know.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question sent in step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: She separates from the second man, and the facts must be investigated before a final ruling.

steps.title: What does 'clarify the matter' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what שמואל wanted to find out by having the matter clarified.
steps.simpleTranslation: What did he mean by 'clarify the matter'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks about שמואל's instruction to clarify the matter. This sets up a back-and-forth to figure out what the investigation would change.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An investigation only makes sense if its result changes the law. So the גמרא needs to find which result would matter: a weak first betrothal or a strong one.

keyTerms.meaning: What is? (asking for the meaning of a phrase)

phrases.english: What is meant by "and clarify the matter"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what the instruction at the end of שמואל's answer in step 16 means.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What result of the investigation would change the law?

steps.title: First suggestion: to cancel the rumor if the first betrothal was weak
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that if the first betrothal turns out to be invalid, the rumor is cancelled and she can stay with the second man.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say he meant this: if it turns out the first man's betrothal was not a real betrothal, we cancel the rumor.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a first possible answer: the investigation is meant to cancel the rumor. This suggestion is about to be challenged.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On this reading, the investigation could free her. If the first קידושין were not valid, the rumor would be set aside and she could stay married to the second man.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (a suggestion the גמרא will usually reject)
The matter is revealed, it becomes clear

phrases.english: If you say that if the matter is revealed
that the betrothal of the first man
was not a proper betrothal,
then we cancel the rumor;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a first proposed answer to the question in step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The investigation is meant to find out whether the first betrothal was weak, which would let the rumor be cancelled.

steps.title: But in שמואל's town they never cancel a rumor
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the first suggestion, because in נהרדעא, שמואל's town, rumors are not cancelled.
steps.simpleTranslation: But נהרדעא is שמואל's town, and there they do not cancel a rumor!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the suggestion from step 18. שמואל follows the practice of נהרדעא, and that practice never cancels a rumor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If שמואל's town never cancels rumors, he would not order an investigation in order to cancel one. So the purpose of 'clarify the matter' must be something else.

phrases.english: But Neharde'a is Shmuel's town,
and there they do not cancel a rumor!
phrases.notes: This refers back to what the גמרא said earlier on the daf about the practice in נהרדעא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the suggestion in step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that שמואל wanted the investigation in order to cancel the rumor.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל's town of נהרדעא does not cancel rumors, so he would not have meant that.

steps.title: Real meaning: if the first betrothal was valid, no גט is needed from the second
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the investigation is meant to show whether the first betrothal was valid. If it was, the second betrothal never took effect, and she needs no גט from the second man.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he meant this: if it turns out the first man's betrothal was a proper betrothal, she does not need a גט from the second man.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the correct meaning of שמואל's instruction. The investigation can only decide whether she needs a גט from the second man.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A married or betrothed woman cannot be betrothed to someone else. So if the first קידושין were valid, the second man's betrothal is meaningless and no גט is needed. Either way, the rumor itself stays in place.
steps.whatToRemember: שמואל never cancels a rumor. The investigation he ordered only decides whether the second man must give a גט.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read this as allowing her to stay with the second man. In every outcome she leaves him. The only open question is whether she needs a גט from him.

phrases.english: Rather, that if the matter is revealed
that the first man's betrothal was a proper betrothal,
she does not need a bill of divorce from the second man.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 19 by giving a different purpose for the investigation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The investigation was meant to cancel the rumor if the first betrothal turned out to be weak.
steps.terutzMaskana: The investigation is meant to show whether the first betrothal was valid. If it was, she needs no גט from the second man.

steps.title: This disagrees with רב הונא: a married woman who accepts a betrothal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that שמואל's ruling disagrees with רב הונא. רב הונא says that a married woman who accepts קידושין from another man is considered betrothed to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: This disagrees with רב הונא, because רב הונא said: if a married woman reached out her hand and accepted a betrothal from another man, she is betrothed to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא compares שמואל with רב הונא and shows that they disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל said that if the first betrothal was valid, she needs no גט from the second man. רב הונא holds that even a known married woman who accepts קידושין needs a גט from the second man. So רב הונא would have required a גט here as well.

keyTerms.meaning: She stretched out her hand (to accept the betrothal)

phrases.english: And this disagrees with Rav Huna,
for Rav Huna said:
A married woman who stretched out her hand
and accepted a betrothal from another man
is betrothed to him,
phrases.notes: He means she is at least possibly betrothed to the second man, so she would need a גט from him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts שמואל's conclusion in step 20 with the opposing view of רב הונא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A married woman who accepts קידושין from another man is considered betrothed to him and needs a גט from him.

steps.title: רב הונא's basis: a wife is not brazen in front of her husband
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא's view comes from רב המנונא, who says that a woman who tells her husband 'you divorced me' is believed, because a wife would not dare to lie to his face.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא's view comes from רב המנונא, because רב המנונא said: a woman who said to her husband 'You divorced me' is believed. There is a presumption that a woman would not be brazen enough to lie in front of her husband.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the source of רב הונא's view: רב המנונא's rule about a wife's believability.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A wife would not openly accept another man's betrothal unless she believed she was free. So her act suggests her first marriage may have ended, which is why she needs a גט from the second man. By the same reasoning, in שמואל's case her acceptance of the second betrothal should weaken the rumor about the first.

keyTerms.meaning: A firm presumption about how people behave
Acts brazenly, lies boldly to someone's face

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל: if the first betrothal was valid, there is no need for a גט from the second man. רב הונא, based on רב המנונא's חזקה: her accepting the second betrothal is taken seriously, so a גט is needed.

phrases.english: This comes from Rav Hamnuna's teaching;
for Rav Hamnuna said:
A woman who said to her husband: "You divorced me"
is believed,
for there is a presumption that a woman is not brazen
in front of her husband.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning behind רב הונא's ruling in step 21.
steps.raayaObject: רב הונא's ruling that a married woman who accepts קידושין needs a גט from the second man
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב המנונא's חזקה that a wife does not lie brazenly in front of her husband

steps.title: שמואל limits רב המנונא's rule to when she speaks in front of her husband
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that שמואל holds רב המנונא's rule only applies when the wife speaks in her husband's presence. When he is not there, she may well dare to lie.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how does the other one (שמואל) deal with this? When רב המנונא's rule was said, it was about a wife speaking in front of her husband. When he is not there, she certainly is brazen enough to lie.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how שמואל can disagree with רב הונא, given רב המנונא's rule that a wife will not lie. It answers that שמואל only accepts that rule when she says it to her husband's face.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא used רב המנונא's rule to say the woman would not accept another man's קידושין if she were really married. שמואל answers that the rule depends on the husband being present. Accepting קידושין from another man happens away from her husband, so she may be lying and the second קידושין may mean nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one: how does the other opinion handle this?
In his presence, to his face
She is brazen, she dares to lie

steps.confusionAlert: שמואל does not reject רב המנונא's rule. He only limits it to cases where the wife speaks in front of her husband.

phrases.english: And the other one?
phrases.notes: This means שמואל, who disagrees with רב הונא.

phrases.english: When Rav Hamnuna's rule was said,
it was in his presence;
not in his presence, she certainly is brazen.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends שמואל against the support for רב הונא brought in step 22
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of a cited principle
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב המנונא's rule seems to show that a married woman would never accept קידושין from another man, so the second קידושין should count.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule only applies when she speaks in front of her husband. Away from him she may lie, so שמואל's ruling stands.

steps.title: What if the investigation gives no clear answer?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the law is if the investigation cannot clearly show whether the first קידושין was valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: If they did not find a clear answer, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question. Until now we assumed the investigation would succeed, but what if it shows nothing for sure?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 20 the investigation was supposed to decide whether the first קידושין was valid. Here the result is unclear, so she may be betrothed to the first man or to the second. This question sets up the rulings that follow.

phrases.english: If they did not find the matter clearly,
phrases.notes: They checked whether the first קידושין was valid but could not tell for sure.

phrases.english: what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא מָצְאוּ דָּבָר עַל בּוּרְיוֹ, מַהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the case where the investigation succeeds to the case where it fails
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What to do with the woman when it stays unclear whether the first קידושין was valid

steps.title: רב הונא: the first man divorces and the second marries, not the reverse
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא rules that the first man must give a גט and then the second man may marry her. The second man may not divorce her so the first can marry her, because people might think the first man is taking back his divorcée after she was betrothed to someone else.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: the first man divorces her and the second man marries her. But the second man divorcing her and the first man marrying her is not allowed. Why? People will come to say that he is taking back his divorcée after she was betrothed to another man.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא answers the question. Since we are unsure, she needs a גט from one man, and only the first man may give it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Either way, one man gives a גט so she is surely free to marry the other. If the first man divorced her, people see him give a גט and the second man marry her, which looks normal. If the order is reversed, onlookers who saw the first man's קידושין, then the second man's קידושין, and then the first man marrying her, will think he divorced her and took her back after she was betrothed to another man, which is forbidden.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that even when the strict law is unclear, the חכמים pick a path that will not look like a sin to onlookers.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
The first divorces, and the second marries.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל מְגָרֵשׁ שֵׁנִי וְנוֹשֵׂא רִאשׁוֹן – לָא.
phrases.english: But the second divorcing and the first marrying is not allowed.
What is the reason?
People will come to say:
he is taking back his divorcée after her betrothal.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: מְגָרֵשׁ רִאשׁוֹן, וְנוֹשֵׂא שֵׁנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised in step 24
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The first man gives a גט and the second man marries her. The reverse is forbidden because it looks like remarrying a divorcée after another man's קידושין.

steps.title: רב שיננא: the reverse order is also allowed
steps.stepSummary: רב שיננא בריה דרב אידי says the second man may also divorce her and the first man marry her. People will not suspect anything, because they will assume the חכמים checked the second קידושין and found it was a mistake.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שיננא בריה דרב אידי said: even the second man divorcing her and the first man marrying her is allowed. People will say: the חכמים looked into the second man's קידושין, and it was a mistaken קידושין.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא disagrees with רב הונא's worry and allows either order.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא feared people would think the first man was taking back his divorcée. רב שיננא says people will explain it differently: they will think the חכמים found the second קידושין was never valid. In that case the first man never divorced her at all, so nothing looks wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: A mistaken קידושין, one that never took effect

steps.whatToRemember: When it is unclear which קידושין is valid, רב הונא allows only the first man to give the גט so the second can marry her. רב שיננא allows either order, because people will assume the second קידושין was found to be a mistake.

phrases.aramaic: רַב שִׁינָּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי אָמַר:
phrases.english: Rav Shinnana son of Rav Idi said:
Even the second divorcing and the first marrying is allowed,
because people will say:
the Rabbis looked into the betrothal,
phrases.notes: He means the second man's קידושין.

phrases.english: and it was a mistaken betrothal.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב שִׁינָּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי אָמַר: אַף מְגָרֵשׁ שֵׁנִי וְנוֹשֵׂא רִאשׁוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב הונא's ruling in step 25
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Either man may give the גט and the other may marry her, since onlookers will assume the second קידושין was found to be a mistake.

steps.title: What if rumors spread about two different men?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks about a woman about whom a rumor of קידושין went out with one man, and then another rumor went out with a second man.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a rumor went out that she was betrothed to this man, and another rumor that she was betrothed to that man, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about a slightly different case. It is setting up the next two steps, where רב פפא (step 28) and אמימר (step 29) answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now, the case had one rumor of קידושין and then a real קידושין to a second man. Now both sides are only rumors. The question is whether this changes the rule about who must give a גט and who may marry her.

keyTerms.meaning: A rumor went out about her (that she was betrothed)
From this one and from that one, meaning two different men

phrases.english: A rumor went out about her
from this man and from that man; what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: יָצָא עָלֶיהָ קוֹל מִזֶּה וּמִזֶּה, מַהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from one rumor plus one real קידושין to a case of two rumors about two men.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether, with two rumors about two men, the earlier rule still applies: the first man divorces and only the second may marry her.

steps.title: רב פפא: the first man divorces and the second marries
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא rules that in this case too, the first man must give a גט and the second man may marry her.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: In this case too, the first man divorces her and the second man marries her.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the question. He says the same rule as before applies: only the second man may marry her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אַף ('also') tells us he is applying רב הונא's earlier ruling (step 25) to the new case. The concern is the same. If the second man divorced her and the first man then married her, people might think the first man was taking back his divorcée after she had been betrothed to someone else.

keyTerms.meaning: This case too (same rule as before)
The first man divorces (gives a גט)

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
In this case too, the first man divorces her
phrases.notes: 'Too' points back to רב הונא's ruling in the earlier case (step 25).

phrases.english: and the second man marries her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 27 by extending רב הונא's rule.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The first man gives a גט and the second man marries her, the same as רב הונא's ruling.

steps.title: אמימר: she is permitted to either man
steps.stepSummary: אמימר disagrees and rules that she is permitted to both men. Either one may give a גט, and then the other may marry her.
steps.simpleTranslation: אמימר said: She is permitted to both of them.
steps.whatsHappening: אמימר gives a different answer from רב פפא. In his view, either man may be the one who marries her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא allows only the second man to marry her. אמימר allows either one, as long as the other gives a גט first. He is not worried that people will think the first man took back his divorcée.

keyTerms.meaning: To the two of them (to either man)

steps.whatToRemember: With two rumors about two men, רב פפא says only the second man may marry her after the first gives a גט. אמימר says either man may marry her once the other gives a גט.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Permitted to both' does not mean she may be married to both men at once. It means either one may marry her after the other gives her a גט.

phrases.english: Ameimar said:
She is permitted to both of them.
phrases.notes: He means to either one of them, after the other man gives her a גט.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer to the question in step 27, disagreeing with רב פפא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Either man may marry her, as long as the other man gives a גט first.
